summary: Enhance your skills with our Targeting Mechanisms for Social Assistance Training Course. Learn effective strategies to improve social support systems today.
lede: Social assistance targeting mechanisms help program teams identify eligible people and assess how accurately selection processes work. For program managers, policy analysts, evaluators and government officials, the course covers poverty and vulnerability assessment, comparison of geographic, demographic and other targeting approaches, and measurement of inclusion and exclusion errors. Participants also develop skills in beneficiary registration, grievance systems and performance monitoring.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals responsible for designing, implementing, managing, or evaluating social assistance programs and their targeting mechanisms.
audience: Program Officers at donor agencies and international
Technical Specialists in social registries and management
modules: Targeting Error Analysis and Correction Strategies
Targeting in Emergency and Crisis Contexts
prerequisites: Participants should have: At least 2 years of experience in social protection, development, or public policy; Basic understanding of poverty measurement and social assistance program concepts; Familiarity with quantitative data analysis and statistical concepts; Experience with program design, implementation, or evaluation; Access to laptop for practical exercises and tool development
